prompt: What are the best youth soccer team ranking sites in the US?
response_text:
Here are some of the best youth soccer team ranking sites in the U.S., with what makes them strong and where to use them. Different sites shine depending on whether you want club-wide rankings, specific age group/team comparison, national coverage, tournament performance, or local insights.

---

## Top U.S. Youth Soccer Ranking Sites

| Site | What It Ranks / Covers | How It Works / Data Sources | Best Use Case | Limitations |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **USYSRankings.com (U.S. Youth Soccer Official Rankings)** | U13–U19 boys & girls club teams nationally | Uses results from verified sources (e.g. MLS NEXT, ECNL), merges performance into a rating system. ([usysrankings.com](https://usysrankings.com/?utm_source=openai)) | Checking top club rankings in elite national leagues; especially useful if your club is in MLS NEXT or ECNL. | Geared toward older age groups; newer or non-elite teams may not appear. |
| **PitchRank** | Teams (U10–U19), boys & girls, all 50 states | Advanced algorithm: looks at wins/losses, margin of victory, strength of opponent; updates weekly. ([pitchrank.io](https://www.pitchrank.io/?utm_source=openai)) | Great for comparing your specific team’s performance, finding detailed team trends. | Teams with fewer cross-state matchups may get undervalued. |
| **Golazo IQ** | U8–U18/National youth teams, both genders | Uses official match results; weighs opponent strength, schedule difficulty, recency, and goal margins. ([golazoiq.com](https://golazoiq.com/rankings/?utm_source=openai)) | If you want age-group-specific team rankings and radar charts for both boys & girls. | Less visibility in younger/very local teams due to limited data. |
| **GotSport Rankings** | Travel teams in U10–U19 across US & Canada | Based on tournament results in GotSport‐hosted events. Teams earn points per placement; flight strength considered. ([pitchrank.io](https://www.pitchrank.io/blog/best-youth-soccer-ranking-websites-2026?utm_source=openai)) | Best if your team plays mostly in GotSport tournaments; to see relative standing across large numbers of teams. | Doesn’t account for head‐to‐head matches outside GotSport; can be biased by regional tournament density. |
| **SoccerWire (Top 100 Clubs)** | Clubs (not individual teams) in ECNL, MLS NEXT, Girls Academy (U13–U19) | Looks at league standings, playoff results, national championship showings, and player advancement. ([pitchrank.io](https://www.pitchrank.io/blog/best-youth-soccer-ranking-websites-2026?utm_source=openai)) | Good for assessing which local clubs have strong track records for development. | Doesn’t tell you about your specific age group within a club or specific team performance. |
| **USARank (SincSports-powered)** | Individual teams U8–U19 across the U.S. | Uses results from SincSports tournaments, recency weighting; weekly updates. ([pitchrank.io](https://www.pitchrank.io/blog/best-youth-soccer-ranking-websites-2026?utm_source=openai)) | Helps gauge where your team fits nationally if you compete in SincSports events. | Only captures tournaments managed by SincSports; record transparency is less than fully open‐source ones. |
| **Elite Rank** | Top 100 boys club teams in various age groups | “EQ system” based on performance metrics; focuses on the highest-performing clubs. ([eliterank.app](https://eliterank.app/rankings/boys-u18?utm_source=openai)) | Use when you want to compare Elite-level clubs in your age group. | Very elite-only; most local/travel-level teams aren’t represented. |
| **National Soccer Network (NSN Top 100)** | Top U.S. youth soccer clubs across platforms (MLS NEXT, ECNL, etc.) | Combines programs from multiple elite circuits; considers results and program prestige. ([nationalsoccernetwork.tv](https://www.nationalsoccernetwork.tv/page/top100boysclubs?utm_source=openai)) | Useful for seeing which clubs are nationally prominent—not just individual teams. | Not focused on smaller clubs; tends to capture big names in elite leagues. |

---

## How to Read & Use These Rankings

These ranking sites can give you insight, but they’re not the whole story. Parents, coaches, and players should also consider:

- **Criteria differences** — Some sites reward tournament finishes, others focus on head-to-head wins, margin of victory, or strength of schedule. ([pitchrank.io](https://www.pitchrank.io/blog/best-youth-soccer-ranking-websites-2026?utm_source=openai))  
- **Geographic bias** — If your region has many tournaments in GotSport or SincSports, or many inter-state matches, your team may get more visibility. If not, you could be underrated.  
- **Age-group variance** — A club may be top 10 overall yet have very strong youth U14s but middle-of-the-pack juniors, or vice versa. Look at your specific age group.  
- **Development vs result focus** — Some sites like SoccerWire emphasize producing players and development, not just wins. Others prioritize match outcomes. ([pitchrank.io](https://www.pitchrank.io/blog/best-youth-soccer-ranking-websites-2026?utm_source=openai))  
- **Latest updates & schedule recency** — Keeping up with weekly/seasonal updates helps avoid outdated data. Sites like PitchRank refresh often. ([pitchrank.io](https://www.pitchrank.io/rankings?utm_source=openai))
